StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Single, and this power leaves Power.on_stack alone, so both sides add on re-application -- PowerCmd.ModifyAmount:236 has no StackType branch and Single means only 'Amount is hidden' (PowerStackType.cs:10-13). Correct, unlike the 15 units that override on_stack to a no-op citing the same StackType (`py audit/tools/power_census.py stack`).

AfterCardEnteredCombat.issue: The owner filter is dropped, which is harmless in single-player, but the SITE is not: C# afflicts from AfterCardEnteredCombat (RingingPower.cs:34-40) and the sim's on_card_entered_combat (hooks.py:402-407) is fired only where the sim happens to call it. Recorded as a gap because the sim's __init__ walks `getattr(owner, 'all_cards', ())` (powers.py:1330) and PlayerCombatState.all_cards is `hand + draw + discard + exhaust` evaluated live (player.py:100-103) -- it does NOT include cards currently in the Play pile, i.e. a card mid-resolution. C# reads PlayerCombatState.AllCards, which is Hand, Draw, Discard, Exhaust AND Play (PlayerCombatState.cs:70-80). So a Ringing applied while a card is mid-play leaves that card unafflicted in the sim and afflicts it in the game. This is PROMPT.md bug class 7 (pile limbo) in its power form. DORMANT: Ringing is applied by an enemy on the enemy's turn, when no player card is mid-play. Named trigger: any player-side or mid-resolution Ringing application. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterSideTurnEnd.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: the player-side leg moved off the sim's Hook.BeforeTurnEnd slot (`on_player_turn_end`) onto `after_player_turn_end`, which combat.py:809 dispatches AFTER `_process_turn_end_cards` and the hand flush -- the sim's port of Hook.AfterTurnEnd (CombatManager.cs:1307), the dispatcher for AbstractModel.AfterSideTurnEnd (Hook.cs:1267-1292). VERIFIED 2026-07-27 by reading combat.py:781-812 and this power's class in powers.py. WAS: the effect ran inside Hook.BeforeTurnEnd, so its order relative to the turn-end card effects, the flush and Stampede's turn-end auto-plays was hook registration order. The registration-order witness is doubly gone: StampedePower also moved, to `after_auto_post_play_phase_entered` (powers.py:1089), which combat.py:789 fires strictly before this slot.

AfterRemoved.maps_to: powers.py:1357-1363 RingingPower._expire clears every Ringing affliction

ShouldPlay.issue: HISTORY vs FLAG. C# answers 'has the owner played a card this turn' by querying CombatManager.History.CardPlaysStarted for entries that HappenedThisTurn; the sim keeps a boolean set from on_card_played. The two differ during a card's own resolution: C#'s history entry is written when the play STARTS (CardModel.cs:1930), so a card auto-played from inside the first card's resolution is already 'after a card this turn' and is blocked, while the sim's flag is set only in on_card_played, AFTER resolution (combat.py:514), so the nested auto-play slips through. Reachable: the sim auto-plays from inside a resolution in several ported places (HellraiserPower powers.py:707-713 on draw, MayhemPower :3572-3583, StampedePower :1025-1041). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

guards.rationale: powers.py:1331 and :1336 both test `card.affliction is None`, so Ringing never overwrites another affliction. Contrast power/tangled, whose C# AfterApplied omits the test and whose sim port adds it.
Omitted; tautology in single-player. The polarity is right: this is an AND predicate and a non-owner must vote true.

guards.what: RingingPower.cs:74 the history query is per-OWNER
guards.rationale: `e.CardPlay.Card.Owner.Creature == base.Owner`; the sim's flag is per-power and there is one player. Equivalent -- the divergence is WHEN the flag is set, recorded on the ShouldPlay entry.

guards.what: RingingPower.cs:47 PowerCmd.Remove -> AfterRemoved does the clearing
guards.rationale: The sim routes the clearing through an overridden _expire (powers.py:1357-1363) that calls super()._expire() last, so the affliction sweep happens on every removal path exactly as C#'s AfterRemoved does. This is the right shape: contrast the units where _expire replaces PowerCmd.Remove and an AfterRemoved would be missed.
